name: Ellen Pea
why: A rock wall beside the highway; no glacier. Way in starts once the gully melts out in late June, so no snow on the line in season.

name: Southeast Ridge
why: Scramble with no glacier; snow is only late May to June neve, before the Jul season starts.

name: Energizer Bunny
why: South-face rock route off the Core approach; no glacier on the line and snow is Aasgard Pass early season.

name: East Gully Route (East Peak)
why: Season is June only and the approach goes up early-season snow slopes to the gully; no glacier there.

name: South Slopes
why: Axe carried into early July for snow patches on the traverse and early-season snow on the descent; no glacier on this scramble.

name: Gorillas Direct
why: Snow below the wall eases by late July to early September per the way-in season; no glacier travel is described but the text is thin, so glacier stays unsure.

name: Improbable Traverse
why: A snow cone sits at the base of the slabs in early season, and the season starts in June; no glacier is described anywhere.

name: North Ridge
why: Lingering snow in the approach gully and shaded notch into early to mid July, with a June season start; no glacier in the text.

name: South Ridge
why: Snow lingers below the notch only into early summer, before the slabs are clear in the Jul season; nothing mentions a glacier.

name: South Ridge
why: The summit gully and shoulder hold snow into June and July, with axe and traction carried.

name: North Face
why: Gully holds snow or verglas into June and the approach gully has early-season snow; the season starts in June.

name: Standard Scramble (off the PCT)
why: Snow in the boot-path gully and on the PCT traverse into June and July in high-snow years, with a June season start.

name: Leche La Vaca
why: The descent slopes hold wet snow into July and the text gives only that timing; no glacier is described but the text is thin.

name: Beckey Route (Southwest Face)
why: The approach gully holds snow into late June and the season starts in June, so snow is in season; the way in is listed as dry from July. No glacier is named anywhere.

name: The Girl Next Door
why: It shares the Beckey approach gully, which has early-season snow; June is in season and the dry window starts in July. No glacier mentioned.

name: Northwest Face
why: The approach gully holds snow into early summer, and the season opens in June. Timing is vague, so the date is a guess at the start of July.

name: Overexposure
why: It uses the Beckey gully, which needs an axe early season; June is in season. Date taken from the sibling route's dry-from-July way in.

name: West Ridge
why: The basin couloir is a snow route in June-July and turns to scree and brush later; the Cave Ridge way is the late-season option. No glacier is described.

name: West Route
why: The high country is not fully snow-free until mid to late July and shaded ground holds snow into midsummer; season starts July. No glacier named.

name: South Route
why: Season opens late May and the gully holds wet snow and avalanche debris into June, so snow is in season until July. No glacier mentioned.

name: Standard Scramble (Appleton Pass / Boulder Lake approach)
why: Snow near the pass and in the summit basin lingers into July and the park advises an axe early; the season opens late June.

name: South Slopes
why: Snowfields into July need an axe, and one way in has steep cirque snow into midsummer; the shortest way in starts late July. Date is the start of August.

name: Tribute to Richard
why: Snow is mentioned only for early or late attempts with no timing, and the season is Jul-Sep. No glacier is described.
